hypotheses.title: Every int range expression rebuilds the same iterator object type from scratch
hypotheses.issue: semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go:resolveRangeExpr calls createIteratorType(t.typeEnv(), semtypes.Int, semtypes.Nil) for every `a ..< b` / `a ... b` expression. createIteratorType builds a fresh MappingDefinition for record {| int value; |}, a ListDefinition for the empty readonly param list, a FunctionDefinition for next(), and an ObjectDefinition. The arguments are constant, so the result is always the same type: object { public function next() returns record {| int value; |}?; }. Each call does a full ObjectDefinition.Define plus many env.typeAtom calls, and each typeAtom call takes the env mutex and inserts into the shared atom table, which also grows the env permanently. On a file with many range loops, this path is about 32% of CPU and about 30% of all allocated bytes. Local type resolution of the module is about 10x slower than it needs to be.

hypotheses.fix_approach: Build the int-range iterator type once per semtypes.Env and reuse it. The prototype adds `intRangeIteratorOnce sync.Once` and `intRangeIterator SemType` to the semtypes env struct. It also adds an exported semtypes.CreateIntRangeIterator(env), which builds the type lazily under the Once, following the existing CreateJSON/CreateIterable predefined-type helpers in core.go. resolveRangeExpr calls the new helper, and createIteratorType moves into semtypes as a private createIterator. The cache has to be per env, not per Context, because each function resolver gets a new semtypes.Context, so a per-context memo would barely help. It also has to be concurrency-safe, because function bodies and modules are resolved in parallel. A sync.Once fits both, and make test-race was clean. Pitfall: env has a freeze mode where atoms created after the freeze go to an ephemeral store. Building the type lazily means it is always first built during compilation, before the freeze, which is fine. An eager build at env creation would also work, but it adds atoms to every env, even ones that never use a range expression. Tests: make test passed apart from one network flake (see setup_notes), and make test-race passed.

+// CreateIntRangeIterator returns the iterator object type produced by an integer

notes: Secondary observations from exploration, not verified as hypotheses: (1) The CFG passes in semantics/internal/cfg (Build, analyzeReachability, analyzeExplicitReturn, analyzeUninitializedVars, analyzeFinalReassignments) spawn one goroutine per function, and each one does a recursive ast.Walk. runtime.newstack/copystack is about 10% of CPU on a file with 20k small functions. Making the work sequential cut CFG Analysis from about 380 ms to about 145 ms on that file, but gave no wall-time gain on multi-module packages. (2) Invalid source that uses a reserved keyword (`limit`) as a variable name took more than 100 s to fail on 2x500 small functions. This looks like pathological parser error recovery and is worth a separate look.
